title: early 2-element design for mobile imaging

collection.source: lens-designs.com, Dan Reiley's collection of optical designs in Zemax format
collection.source_basis: The .zmx file is the direct source for the surface table: radii, thicknesses, glasses, clear semi-diameters, conic constants and aspheric terms are read from it. The collection's summary sheet, where it lists this input, is the independent check of the first-order values.
collection.source_revision: site snapshot read on 2026-11-27; the collection states no version of its own

original_publication.reference: named in the input's file name

collection.attribution: Prescription from lens-designs.com (photographic-primes), file EP1357414A1_ex1.zmx. The collection states that every file carries the MIT licence unless its own Notes section says otherwise; this file carries no Notes section.
collection.contributor: Prepared for the lens-designs collection through JunLin615
collection.redistribution: The collection states the MIT licence for its files (note-on-ip page) and that the designs themselves are public domain, being transcriptions of patent or journal publications. The notice is committed at licenses/LensDesigns-MIT.txt.

aperture_validity.basis: The file marks this surface as the stop and its clear semi-diameter is the smallest of the system, so the plate limits the beam.
aperture_validity.consequence: The Project is eligible for stop-dependent evaluation, but no pupil sample or illumination result is recorded, so no stop-dependent match is claimed.
aperture_validity.satisfaction_basis: No pupil sample or illumination measurement is recorded.

spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: DERIVED: the file's WAVM lines are air wavelengths at the reference environment; each is converted once to vacuum with the engine's own air model
spectrum.wavelength_precision: Vacuum nanometres, full precision, as the engine evaluates them.

continuous_coverage_nm.note: The file states its sampling wavelengths only; it states no operating band.

back_focal_length_mm.definition: Paraxial distance from the final surface vertex to the rear focal point

total_track_mm.definition: First surface vertex to the image plane along the axis

effective_focal_length_mm.basis: SOURCE_STATED: the collection's summary sheet for this input

engine_check.method: Thick-lens ABCD through the committed Project at the primary wavelength

comparison.rule: per quantity: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * scale, raised to half a printed unit where the source prints fewer digits than that rule can resolve

f_number.definition: Image-space f-number, from the file's FNUM line with type flag 0

stop_opening_diameter_mm.definition: Diameter of the aperture stop's clear opening as the file states it

field.definition: Image-space field heights, from the file's FTYP and YFLN lines

materials.policy: Glasses the file names are taken from the published catalog when the engine resolves the name; a ___BLANK glass is defined from the nd and vd the file states, as recorded here.

model_glasses.basis: SOURCE_STATED (nd, vd). The file states only nd and vd, so the record solves a three-term Sellmeier through the vacuum C, d and F lines with the stated Abbe number and a normal-glass partial dispersion of 0.60.

SOURCE_STATED (nd, vd). The file states only nd and vd, so the record solves a three-term Sellmeier through the vacuum C, d and F lines with the stated Abbe number and a normal-glass partial dispersion of 0.60.

approximations.description: The file states model glasses by nd and vd only. Each is modelled as a three-term Sellmeier solved through the vacuum C, d and F lines with the stated Abbe number and a normal-glass partial dispersion of 0.60; the d-line index is exact.
The file carries surface solves (thickness or aperture); the values stored in the file are the solved ones and are transcribed as such, without re-solving.
Aspheric terms are carried as the even polynomial coefficients a4..a18 the format holds; the file states no odd term for these surfaces.

evidence_notes: The file states 5 surfaces in 2 elements and 1 aperture stop(s); the import reproduces that decomposition.
The collection's summary prints an EFL of 3.33 mm against the engine's 3.321175 mm; the comparison and its tolerance are in first_order.engine_check.comparison.

The 1 sources sit on the lens axis 100 mm before the first vertex and emit along it; the image plane is at 5.419780 mm from that vertex, the paraxial rear focal point of the committed Project (exit vertex 3.600000 mm plus a back focal length of 1.819780 mm).
